A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BrainOmni and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Reordered appendix sections and relocated analyses can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original downstream classification, cross-device reconstruction, pretraining analyses, and ablation results, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: V2 reports original downstream and reconstruction results, revised appendix experiments, and an additional loss-component ablation.

M1.justification: The two-stage BrainTokenizer/BrainOmni architecture, Sensor Encoder, four-layer RVQ, reconstruction losses, and masked-token training remain unchanged. V2 clarifies per-window cross-attention and documents the downstream classifier; these disclosures do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: V2 adds MEG-MMI depression classification using adolescents' MEG recordings during mood induction, increasing downstream classification coverage from ten datasets to eleven (Tables 1 and 3; Appendix I). Pretraining datasets, previous downstream tasks, and unseen-device scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: FAMED, a MEG-specific model, is added to the existing ASD74 and SomatoMotor comparisons and the new MEG-MMI comparison in Table 3. All previous comparison methods remain, making this a focused comparator addition.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation changes from three-fold cross-validation to five-fold evaluation; v2 Appendix D specifies rotating subject splits and a fixed official test-set exception for TUAB/TUEV. Downstream batch size changes from 64 to 128, AdamW betas from [0.9, 0.95] to [0.9, 0.99], and warmup ratio from 0.05 to 0.1. AD65 segments change from 7,013 to 5,349 and PhysioNet-MI from 19,571 to 9,837; Table 3 drops F1 reporting. The new loss ablation separately introduces four frequency/PCC-loss combinations.

E4.justification: V2 Section 5.2 and Table 7 add a focused ablation of frequency-domain and PCC losses, holding time-domain and commitment losses present. It examines collapse, spectral reconstruction, and waveform artifacts. Existing modality, sensor-embedding, source-compression, frozen-backbone, and visualization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 reports mean and standard deviation over three fold runs using seed 42. V2 reports these over ten runs from five folds and two seeds, identified as 42 and 3407 in Appendix D. This expands the reported sources of variability while retaining the same uncertainty-summary practice.

E6.justification: Downstream and appendix ablation scores are extensively replaced under revised settings. For example, Table 2 changes BrainOmni_base's PhysioNet-MI BACC from 0.439 ± 0.011 to 0.590 ± 0.022, with CBraMod now ranked first at 0.595 ± 0.015. These are revised-protocol results, not established same-setting gains. MEG-MMI, FAMED, and loss-ablation results are added, while Table 3 F1 results disappear. Table 4 reconstruction values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–17, the source-estimation assumptions and derivations in Appendix B, and the mathematical formulation of BrainOmni are retained. The new preprocessing pseudocode documents implementation rather than adding a theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unified EEG–MEG pretraining, physical sensor encoding, spatiotemporal tokenization, cross-device generalization, and benefits from joint training. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 explains how frequency loss improves spectral reconstruction but can introduce impulses, and how PCC loss mitigates them. Appendix A newly acknowledges that domain-specific models may outperform BrainOmni on individual tasks. Appendix F.1 also removes the earlier SomatoMotor compression-penalty qualification following the revised results.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands reproducibility information with the pooling/MLP classifier, preprocessing Algorithm 1, rereferencing details, split and seed handling, training times, and throughput. The abstract replaces a future-release promise with a repository link stating that code and checkpoints are available. Downstream hyperparameters are revised, although parameter counts for four non-pretrained baselines are removed from Tables 2–3.

R1.justification: V2 adds the cited FAMED work by Hirano et al. and the MEG-MMI dataset by Liuzzi et al. The existing related-work discussion and positioning relative to earlier foundation models remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 moves the Sensor Encoder ablation into Section 5, reorders analysis subsections and appendices, expands implementation explanations, and adds acknowledgements and a conference header. Most introductory, methodological, theoretical, and concluding prose is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 7 and Algorithm 1, expands Table 1, and restructures Table 3 with a new dataset column and baseline row while removing F1 columns. Figure 3's existing panels are reordered, its caption specifies L1 loss, and several figures and appendix tables move. The overall visual format and architecture diagrams remain stable.

improvement.justification: V2 provides stronger support for the existing work through an additional clinical MEG evaluation, a MEG-specific comparator, a targeted loss ablation, and evaluation across two seeds. Expanded preprocessing, classifier, split, runtime, and access information improves reproducibility. These are useful incremental gains, partly offset by losing F1 results and baseline parameter counts; the changed evaluation settings prevent interpreting higher scores as direct performance improvements.
